I got a traditional deck like this https://shinpaideshou.files.wordpress.com/2010/11/hanafuda-all1.jpg in a very nice wooden box for about 20 euro

I believe Koi-Koi is one of the more popular games you can play with hanafuda

Each round, each player is dealt 8 cards, and there are 8 cards placed face up between the players that are "up for grabs"
The players take turns, and each turn you play one card from your hand and then flip one card over from the top of the deck of undealt cards.
If the card you played is the same season/flower (e.g. January = pine, February = plum blossom) as one of the face-up cards, both of those cards are added to your "stash". If there are no matches, the card is added to the field of face-up cards. The same applies for the card that you flip up from the deck.

The point of the game is to make Yaku, or special combinations of cards. There are a whole bunch of different combinations that you'll have to memorize or refer to. Each combination is worth a certain number of points corresponding to how difficult it is to get those yaku.

There's one more layer of complexity, though. After a turn, if you do manage to complete a yaku, you get the choice to continue playing in the hopes of making more yaku and earning more points, or ending the round then and there. This is classic risk vs. reward, as choosing to continue playing means your opponent has a chance to steal the round and deny you any points you would have otherwise earned.

There are a few other nuances, but I suggest trying it out for yourself! There are free hanafuda apps where you can play against AI, and there are also online versions as well!

Edit: Here's an online game and here's a simple guide to get started

You can see how there's a lot of depth and strategy involved. You have to keep in mind your best possible plays while keeping your opponent in check (denying yaku if necessary) and playing around probabilities (what cards/seasons have or have not been played yet)
